hints: Focus on the carbonyl group in pentan-2-one, the C=O carbon is electron poor and is where a nucleophile will attack.
Identify the two groups already on that carbonyl carbon, a methyl group and a propyl group, and remember the incoming nucleophile is an ethyl group, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^-$.
Join all three carbon groups onto the same carbon with the new OH to build a tertiary alcohol, then match that skeleton to the diagrams.
walkthrough:
**Spot the electrophile and nucleophile**

Think simply: the C=O carbon loves electrons to be given to it, and R- loves to give them.

Here the electrophile is pentan-2-one:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
The nucleophile is the ethyl anion:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^-$$

**Do the nucleophilic addition to the C=O**

The ethyl anion forms a new C-C bond to the carbonyl carbon, and the pi bond breaks to give $\text{O}^-$.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(O}^-\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Protonate to get the alcohol**

Adding $\text{H}^+$ turns $\text{O}^-$ into OH, but the carbon skeleton does not change.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{C(O}^-\text{)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$
This is a tertiary alcohol with methyl, ethyl and propyl groups on the C-OH carbon, which is 3-methylpentan-3-ol.

options.A: This is pentan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It shows only the original ketone skeleton with H added to the carbonyl carbon. It misses the key C-C bond forming step where the ethyl group joins on.
options.B: This shows the central C-OH bonded to $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. That is exactly $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_2\text{CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, the tertiary alcohol from ethyl addition to pentan-2-one.
options.C: This is 2-methylpentan-2-ol, with two methyl groups on the C-OH carbon. That would come from addition of $\text{CH}_3^-$ instead of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2^-$. It confuses the ethyl nucleophile with a methyl nucleophile.
options.D: This is heptan-4-ol, a secondary alcohol with two propyl groups on the C-OH carbon. That would require addition of a propyl nucleophile to butanal, not addition of ethyl to pentan-2-one.
